chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ali al-Qummi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The expansiveness of the shirt (garment) and the growth of hair in the nose is a safety from leprosy.
Then he (peace be upon him) said: Have you not heard the words of the poet: 'And you will not see my shirt except as wide of the collar and the sleeves'.

key_terms.الْجَيْبِ: The chest or collar area of a garment
key_terms.الْجُرُبَّانِ: A type of loose, wide garment or shirt
key_terms.الْيَدِ: The sleeve or arm area of a garment

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of safety from leprosy according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies a broad garment (jurbban) and nasal hair as indicators of protection from leprosy, linking physical attributes to divine safeguarding. He reinforces this by citing a poet’s verse describing a shirt wide in the chest and sleeves, illustrating how outward appearance was historically interpreted as a sign of health and divine favor in early Islamic medical and cultural contexts.
